To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the core of the cooperative game of exchange is not necessarily monotonic, but is monotonic in the presence of barriers to trade, and that the core of exchange with barriers to trade is not necessarily monotonicaly increasing in the number of agents, but is monotone increasing in the number in the absence of barriers to trade.

(1) the core of a trade game with a barrier to trade may be nonmonotonic; (2) the core of an exchange game with a barrier may be nonmonon- tonic; (3) the core of any trade game with a middleman may be nonmonoton- ic; (4) the core of the trade game with a single middleman is monotonic; (5) the core of some exchange games with a middleman is nonmonotonic.

1) the core may be empty for a simple exchange economy with two agents and three commodities; 2) the core is nonempty if the economy satisfies a certain monotonicity condition, but may be empty if the economy fails this condition; and 3) a nonmonotonicity property of the core is due to a nonmonotone relationship between the core of the economy and the core of the subgame obtained by restricting the economy to a subset of agents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the core is nonmonotonic, and if so, what is the nature of the nonmonotonicity?

the following questions. What are the implications of the existence of barriers to trade for the structure of the core? How are the core and the set of stable outcomes affected by the existence of barriers?
the following problem: given a set of agents and a set of barriers to trade among these agents, find the core of the resulting exchange economy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the barriers to trade are a major factor in the development of the international trade system.
, in a world where there are barriers to trade, the core may be empty, and that if the core is not empty, it need not be unique.
there exists a large and growing body of evidence that the barriers to trade in the world economy have declined in the last decade.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that the core may be nonmonotonic with respect to the addition of agents and the introduction of barriers to trade.
, for any set of traders and any set of possible barriers to trade, there is a core that depends on the barriers and on the set of traders.
the existence of barriers to trade and the existence of middlemen may lead to a nonmonotonic core.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the core of an economy can be non-monotone in the set of feasible coalitional trades.
the core of a trade network game may not be monotonic in the sense of Shapley [1969].
barriers to trade can have a nontrivial effect on the core of a market game.
